lessonRef.unitTitle: PF5 — Financial Investing: Risk, Return, and Why Diversification Matters
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: how inflation changes real returns

objective: Convert a fictional nominal return into a real return by adjusting for inflation, and state what the money will actually buy at the end of the year.
scenario: A fictional investment of $4,000 returns 5.4% over one simulated year while prices in that simulated economy rise 3.1%. All figures are invented for this exercise.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional return and inflation figures in these directions

tasks.directions: The fictional investment grows 5.4% in the year. Prices rise 3.1% over the same year, so a basket costing $1.00 in January costs $1.031 in December.

prompts.text: What is the investment worth at the end of the year in plain dollars?
What is that end-of-year amount worth in January prices? Round to the nearest cent.
What is the real gain — the increase in what the money can buy?

tasks.directions: Now express the same result as a rate.

prompts.text: What is the real rate of return? Round to one decimal place.
If inflation had instead been 6.0%, would this investment have gained or lost purchasing power?
choices: Neither; it would have broken even

prompts.text: The account balance rose by $216 and the investor got $89.23 better off. Explain where the other $126.77 went, and say why a statement showing only the balance can be misleading.

remediation: If the real return comes out as exactly 2.3%, the two rates are being subtracted. Subtraction is a good estimate but not the calculation: divide 1.054 by 1.031 and subtract 1 to get the real figure.
extension: Compute the nominal return this investment would have needed to deliver a 4% real return at 3.1% inflation, and say how far that is above 7.1%.
